# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.
#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.
**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Getting the stack trace.** Console output truncates the exception to its message; `-p:ErrorLog=out.sarif` preserves the full description, including the stack trace and an `ISymbol:` context line naming the offending type:

```
dotnet build -p:ErrorLog=out.sarif
```

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

[mp-repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30408133/mp-repro.zip)

story.summary: The fix stops the generator and analyzer from crashing when a closed generic struct comes from a referenced assembly. The crash came from indexing `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` on symbols loaded from metadata. Two such sites now use null-safe lookups: line 985 through a new `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` helper, and line 1077 through `FirstOrDefault()`. The analyzer's report delegate is also wrapped so that any diagnostic without a source location in the current compilation is silently dropped. Three tests compile a defining assembly to a metadata-only image, then check two things: no diagnostics, and the resolver hint name is generated. The change also adds two doc paragraphs and an unrelated runtime change in `MessagePackSecurity.GetEqualityComparer<T>`.
story.why: REQ-2283: `IndexOutOfRangeException` (CS8785/AD0001) on a closed generic value type from a referenced assembly. The generator fails, so no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver` is emitted.
touches_beyond_requirement: src/MessagePack/MessagePackSecurity.cs: `GetEqualityComparer<T>` now returns `EqualityComparer<T>.Default` for `string` even when `HashCollisionResistant` is on. This is runtime behaviour on the untrusted-data path and unrelated to the generator bug.

TypeCollector.cs line 239 / 1444-1450: a global filter now drops every analyzer diagnostic whose location is not in a syntax tree of the compilation. That includes diagnostics created with a null location for source types, not only metadata members.
README.md and doc/analyzers/MsgPack004.md: new user-facing documentation of the suppression policy.
story.confidence_overview: Medium that the crash is fixed for the tested shapes. The tests reproduce the issue's record-struct case using a real metadata image and check that the resolver is emitted. Low certainty that every crash site is covered: the issue names a third `[0]` site (old line 735) that this diff does not show touching. High confidence that the `MessagePackSecurity` change is out of scope and weakens hash-collision protection on runtimes without randomized string hashing.

Adding AppResolver changes the resolver discovery path so implicit resolver generation from the issue is not tested.

claims.text: Docs: README and the MsgPack004 docs state that diagnostics for members of types from referenced assemblies are reported only by the defining project. This describes the new filter rather than the crash fix.

breaker.reason: C12 cites README.md lines 1639-1643 and claims 'This describes the new filter rather than the crash fix', which mischaracterizes and over-cites README.md line 1641: line 1641 explicitly documents that closed generic types defined in a referenced assembly (including generic value types and record structs such as Item<int>) can be used as members of [MessagePackObject] types, directly describing the scenario enabled by the crash fix rather than only the diagnostic filter.

claims.text: The `BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull` diagnostic now gets its location from `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation`. It no longer casts `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]`, so a metadata property does not throw there.

breaker.reason: Checked TypeCollector.cs line 985. BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull now obtains its location via GetPropertyIdentifierLocation(item) instead of indexing DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] and casting to PropertyDeclarationSyntax, preventing an exception on metadata properties, and C2 accurately notes that no test in the diff exercises this path.

claims.text: New helper `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` returns the property identifier location when the first syntax reference is a `PropertyDeclarationSyntax`, and null otherwise (including metadata symbols).
claims.requirement_quote: that collection is empty for a metadata symbol

breaker.reason: Checked TypeCollector.cs lines 1429-1434. GetPropertyIdentifierLocation uses property.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax() as PropertyDeclarationSyntax followed by ?.Identifier.GetLocation(), returning the identifier location when the first syntax reference is a PropertyDeclarationSyntax and null otherwise (including empty DeclaringSyntaxReferences on metadata symbols).

claims.text: Scope: the `MessagePackSecurity.GetEqualityComparer<T>` change, which bypasses the hash-collision-resistant comparer for `string`, is unrelated to the requirement. No test in the diff exercises it.

breaker.reason: Checked src/MessagePack/MessagePackSecurity.cs lines 134-139 and the test diff. The typeof(T) == typeof(string) branch returns EqualityComparer<T>.Default before checking HashCollisionResistant, bypassing GetHashCollisionResistantEqualityComparer<T>() for strings, is unrelated to REQ-2283, and has no test in the diff.

claims.text: The `MemberNeedsKey` diagnostic now gets its location via `DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()`. It no longer indexes `[0]`, so building it for a metadata member yields a null location instead of throwing.

breaker.reason: Checked TypeCollector.cs line 1077 and GenericsFormatterTests.cs lines 507, 551, 590, and 653. Line 1077 replaces item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] with item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?, yielding a null Location? argument to Diagnostic.Create instead of throwing IndexOutOfRangeException on metadata members. Because lines 1075-1077 construct the Diagnostic before the accessibility check (line 1078) and outside this.reportDiagnostic?.Invoke (line 1080), all three named tests execute line 1077 on metadata struct members (including compiler-generated auto-property backing fields) when MessagePackGenerator runs at line 653.

claims.text: When an analyzer report callback is supplied, it is wrapped so that diagnostics are forwarded only if their location is in source and in a syntax tree of the current compilation; all others are dropped.

breaker.reason: Lines 239 and 1444-1450 of TypeCollector.cs wrap a non-null reportAnalyzerDiagnostic callback in ReportIfLocatedInCompilation, forwarding diagnostics only when diagnostic.Location.IsInSource and this.compilation.ContainsSyntaxTree(diagnostic.Location.SourceTree) hold. However, whether any other TypeCollector constructor sets this.reportDiagnostic and whether the named test ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember actually supplies a non-null analyzer callback cannot be verified from the diff alone because CSharpSourceGeneratorVerifier<MessagePackGenerator> (VerifyCS on line 7 of GenericsFormatterTests.cs) is not shown in the diff, and MessagePackGenerator itself runs with reportAnalyzerDiagnostic == null.

breaker.reason: Lines 590-626 of GenericsFormatterTests.cs verify that MyGenericStruct<T> with an unkeyed public property in a metadata assembly does not crash MessagePackGenerator (run directly at line 653). However, whether this test exercises and codifies the new analyzer diagnostic suppression in ReportIfLocatedInCompilation depends on whether VerifyCS.Test (CSharpSourceGeneratorVerifier<MessagePackGenerator>, line 7 and line 638) also registers MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer, which is defined in code not shown in the diff.

claims.text: Helper `RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync` runs the analyzer+generator verifier, which fails on any unexpected diagnostic such as AD0001/CS8785. It then runs the generator directly, asserting no warning-or-worse diagnostics and that the expected resolver hint name exists.

breaker.reason: Lines 651-658 of GenericsFormatterTests.cs run MessagePackGenerator directly via CSharpGeneratorDriver, asserting no warning-or-worse diagnostics (covering CS8785) and checking expectedResolverHintName. However, whether VerifyCS.Test on lines 638-648 runs MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer in addition to MessagePackGenerator (and would surface AD0001) depends on CSharpSourceGeneratorVerifier<MessagePackGenerator> (line 7), whose definition is not in the diff.

refusals.what: `GetEqualityComparer<T>` returns the default (non-collision-resistant) comparer for strings even in untrusted-data mode.
refusals.why: Weakens hash-collision DoS protection on the untrusted-input deserialization path, notably on .NET Framework where string hashes are not randomized.

refusals.what: Unrelated runtime change bundled into a source-generator crash fix.
refusals.why: Not required by REQ-2283 and not covered by any test in the diff.

refusals.what: Analyzer diagnostics without a location in the current compilation are now silently dropped, and the docs declare this as policy.
refusals.why: Changes which analyzer diagnostics users see. That is a user-visible analyzer behaviour decision beyond fixing the crash.

findings.description: Claim C6 disputed: ClosedGenericRecordStruct_FromMetadataReference does not reproduce the issue's App repro verbatim: lines 575-576 of GenericsFormatterTests.cs add [GeneratedMessagePackResolver] partial class AppResolver { }, whereas the issue's App repro contains only Cmd and relies on implicit GeneratedMessagePackResolver generation. Adding AppResolver changes the resolver discovery path so implicit resolver generation from the issue is not tested.

Claim C12 disputed: C12 cites README.md lines 1639-1643 and claims 'This describes the new filter rather than the crash fix', which mischaracterizes and over-cites README.md line 1641: line 1641 explicitly documents that closed generic types defined in a referenced assembly (including generic value types and record structs such as Item<int>) can be used as members of [MessagePackObject] types, directly describing the scenario enabled by the crash fix rather than only the diagnostic filter.

With `HashCollisionResistant` (the `UntrustedData` setting), string keys now use `EqualityComparer<string>.Default`. On .NET Framework / netstandard hosts, `string.GetHashCode` is not randomized per process by default, so the comment is wrong there. This reopens hash-flooding DoS on dictionaries/sets with string keys. Static check S6 reports 'pass' but misses this. The change is unrelated to the requirement and untested.

The filter drops every diagnostic whose location is `Location.None`, not just those for metadata members. Any existing diagnostic created with a null location for a source type is now silently suppressed. Examples: a `GetIdentifierLocation`/`GetParameterListLocation` that returns null, or a type-level diagnostic with no location. This is a user-visible analyzer behaviour change.

The issue lists three `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites (old lines 735, 1009, 1101). The diff shows only two being changed (985, 1077); the third is not visible. The report filter at 239 does not prevent an index exception thrown while building a diagnostic, so another metadata shape could still crash.
The `UnkeyedMember` test pins down the policy decision that consumers get no warning about unkeyed members of a referenced type. That is a design choice beyond the bug fix, now locked in by a test.

Returning EqualityComparer<T>.Default unconditionally when typeof(T) == typeof(string) before checking HashCollisionResistant introduces a HashDoS security regression on .NET Framework (netstandard2.0 / net472), where string.GetHashCode() is NOT randomized per process by default unless UseRandomizedStringHashAlgorithm is enabled in app config. Under MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData, deserializing string-keyed dictionaries on .NET Framework will no longer use SipHash collision-resistant hashing, and custom MessagePackSecurity subclasses overriding protected virtual GetHashCollisionResistantEqualityComparer<T>() are bypassed for string, also contradicting the XML doc on lines 130-131.

In the same ternary expression as the fixed MemberNeedsKey call (line 1077), the true branch calls derivedKeyAttribute.GetSyntax(this.cancellationToken).GetLocation() unconditionally before the accessibility check (line 1078) and outside reportDiagnostic?.Invoke (line 1080). If a closed generic value type from a referenced metadata assembly has any member annotated with an attribute derived from KeyAttribute, derivedKeyAttribute comes from metadata and has no syntax (ApplicationSyntaxReference is null), so line 1076 will throw NullReferenceException and still crash both MessagePackGenerator (CS8785, omitting the resolver) and MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer (AD0001). Additionally, REQ-2283 noted three DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] sites in GetObjectInfo (3.1.8 lines 735, 1009, 1101, mapping to ~711, 985, 1077) and only two (985, 1077) were updated.

ReportIfLocatedInCompilation filters diagnostics by diagnostic.Location.IsInSource rather than checking whether the analyzed type belongs to this.compilation.Assembly. Consequently, valid diagnostics on types declared in the current source compilation are silently dropped whenever a location helper returns null (producing Location.None). For example, on a positional record in the current compilation with [MessagePackObject] public record R([property: Key((string)null!)] int X), the property's declaring syntax is ParameterSyntax rather than PropertyDeclarationSyntax, so GetPropertyIdentifierLocation (line 1434) returns null, BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull (line 985) gets Location.None, and ReportIfLocatedInCompilation silently drops the diagnostic.
